projects.name: Children of Ur

badge.label: Archived code · game server still up

projects.summary: A browser MMO that rebuilt Glitch in Dart and called itself a spinoff, with new areas and updated storylines alongside the original world.

facts.label: Client
facts.text: Dart, compiled to JavaScript, in the browser. No Flash.

facts.label: Server and rules
facts.text: Dart server and auth server; game systems rewritten from the original ActionScript and data rather than running Tiny Speck's server code.

facts.label: Platform
facts.text: Web browser (its page lists Safari and Edge as unsupported). The client has phone and tablet layouts and a touch joystick.

facts.label: Licence and code
facts.text: Client and server are MIT on GitHub (client 74 stars). Last client commit 2019-02-22; repositories archived.

facts.label: Status
facts.text: Released alphas up to 1.5.1. The website answers with an error, but the game client at play.childrenofur.com still loads and its game server reported a player online when checked on 2026-10-26. A 2019 headline reports the team joining forces with Eleven.

facts.label: How to play
facts.text: The browser client at play.childrenofur.com still connects to a running server; whether new players can still sign up was not tested. In August 2026 one developer published a local Docker setup that runs the archived code on your own machine.

facts.label: Team
facts.text: Size not published.

projects.name: Eleven (Eleven Giants)
projects.summary: A volunteer effort to get the released Glitch code running again, so the game looks and plays exactly as it did, with early help from Tiny Speck.

facts.label: Client
facts.text: The original Flash client, with plans to reduce the reliance on Flash later.

facts.label: Server and rules
facts.text: A Node.js server rebuilds the missing layer between client and server and runs Tiny Speck's original server JavaScript (GSJS).

facts.label: Platform
facts.text: The original Flash client ran in a web browser. How testers run it since Flash reached end of life in 2020 is not documented publicly, and no phone version is mentioned.

facts.label: Licence and code
facts.text: eleven-server and eleven-gsjs are MIT on GitHub (48 and 21 stars). The README says further components needed to start the game are not public. Last non-automated commit 2020-06-12.

facts.label: Status
facts.text: Alpha testing began in December 2014 with 13 players, 31 by January 2015. The website answered with an error today; the forum is online. A player reported in 2023 that the game was broken and unattended (community report).

facts.label: How to play
facts.text: Invite only: the last news post (August 2019) opened an interest list and admitted players in small batches.

facts.label: Team
facts.text: About 28 volunteers listed on the team page.

projects.name: Odd Giants
projects.summary: An online multiplayer remake built in Unity that aims to bring back most of the old game plus new features of its own, with regular releases and community events.

facts.label: Client
facts.text: Unity desktop application (about 2 GB download).

facts.label: Server and rules
facts.text: Own online servers. Server code is not public, so whether it uses Tiny Speck's server code is unknown.

facts.label: Platform
facts.text: A desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux; no phone or browser version. A Steam release is planned.

facts.label: Licence and code
facts.text: Closed source; no public repository found.

facts.label: Status
facts.text: Version 0.19.0 released 2026-08-02; regular patch notes since 2021; 3,382 accounts reported by its API, and players active every day on its public activity feed.

facts.label: How to play
facts.text: Free account, then download. The FAQ says payment is not required to play; Patreon is optional, and future premium accounts would be cosmetic only.

facts.label: Team
facts.text: A small team of developers and artists; size not published.

projects.name: Groddle Afternoon
projects.summary: This project. A web game that rebuilds Glitch rule by rule from Tiny Speck's released code and art, played solo in your browser or multiplayer (built and tested locally, not online yet), and fills the gaps from players' Snaps and recordings.

facts.label: Client
facts.text: PixiJS 8 in the browser, with sharp 3x art on high-resolution screens. No Flash, nothing to install.

facts.label: Server and rules
facts.text: The original server code (GSJS) is mined as the design reference and its rules are rewritten in modern JavaScript. Solo needs no server and saves in your browser. Multiplayer adds accounts and server saves on the site, and a small Go server that decides what players share: quoins, rocks, races, Rook fights and trades.

facts.label: Platform
facts.text: Web browser on a desktop computer, played with the keyboard. No touch controls yet, so not on phones.

facts.label: Licence and code
facts.text: MIT code on GitHub in three repositories: the game, the realtime server and the site. Uses only Tiny Speck's CC0 art, sound and code, plus art and sound made fresh where nothing survives; no Glitch logo or trademark.

facts.label: Status
facts.text: In development and not online yet. The source is public on GitHub, and multiplayer is built and tested locally, but there is no public server and no players yet.

facts.label: How to play
facts.text: Not online yet: run it locally from GitHub. Solo play is static files from the game repository and needs no account; multiplayer also needs the site and the realtime server, with accounts made in the game with an email and a password.

facts.label: Team
facts.text: A one-person project.
